description: Light-emitting diode: a single PN-junction electroluminescent emitter, orderable as such, whose primary spec is optical output versus forward current, with a forward voltage. Covers visible indicator LEDs, high-brightness/illumination white LEDs, multi-color/RGB LEDs, and infrared (IR) and ultraviolet (UV-A/B/C) emitters, in SMD and through-hole packages. The dictionary carries TWO parallel optical vocabularies and a part populates exactly one: a PHOTOMETRIC set (luminous intensity in cd, luminous flux in lm - visible parts, weighted by the eye's response) and a RADIOMETRIC set (radiant intensity in W/sr, radiant flux in W - IR/UV parts, which the eye cannot see). Out of scope as separate families: laser diodes (add threshold current, slope efficiency, coherence), LED driver ICs (a switching regulator - the LED is its load), photodiodes/phototransistors (receivers), and optocouplers (emitter+detector systems). Synthesized from a 20-datasheet corpus across Kingbright, Lite-On, Vishay, Wurth, Cree, ams-OSRAM, Nichia, Samsung, Everlight, Luminus, and Seoul Viosys.

parameters.name: Forward voltage
parameters.hint: The forward voltage drop at a stated forward current (attach I_F) and, for a colored/multi-die part, a stated EMITTER die. Array over I_F - datasheets tabulate VF at several drive currents (e.g. 350/700/1000/1500/2000 mA) and it rises with current. A blue/green (InGaN) die runs ~3 V, a red/amber (AlGaInP) die ~2 V, a UV-C die 5-6.5 V. Store the value at each printed point; carry the junction/solder temperature as a T_SP/T_A condition when given.

parameters.name: Forward current (DC)
parameters.hint: The maximum continuous DC forward current (an absolute-maximum rating; set limitClass absolute_max), in amperes (mA normalized: 30 mA is 0.03; a 2 A power LED is 2). The recommended/nominal operating current at which optical specs are measured is a separate recommended-class value or a condition on the optical parameters. Often derated above a stated ambient/solder temperature - carry the derating knee in conditionsVerbatim.

parameters.name: Peak (pulsed) forward current
parameters.hint: The maximum pulsed forward current (absolute_max), in amperes, valid only for a stated pulse width and duty cycle - attach PULSE_WIDTH (s) and DUTY conditions (e.g. 1/10 duty, 0.1 ms pulse). Higher than the DC rating because the junction has time to cool between pulses.

parameters.name: Surge forward current
parameters.hint: A single-event non-repetitive surge current the die survives (absolute_max), for a stated short pulse (attach PULSE_WIDTH, e.g. tp <= 10 us). Distinct from the repetitive peak_forward_current.

parameters.name: Reverse voltage
parameters.hint: An LED is not built to be reverse-biased. Two distinct senses distinguished by limitClass: the absolute-maximum reverse voltage rating (absolute_max, typically 5 V) and, on some parts, a guaranteed minimum reverse breakdown (characterized, at a stated reverse test current). Some emitters state 'not designed for reverse operation' - record that verbatim rather than a number.

parameters.name: Reverse current
parameters.hint: Reverse leakage current at a stated reverse voltage (attach V_R), in amperes (uA normalized: 10 uA is 1e-5). Note some power/UV parts instead print an 'allowable reverse current' as an absolute-maximum rating in mA - the limitClass disambiguates a leakage spec from a rating.

parameters.name: Power dissipation
parameters.hint: The maximum power the package can dissipate (absolute_max), in watts (mW normalized: 150 mW is 0.15). Bounded by junction temperature and thermal resistance; derated above a reference temperature.

parameters.name: Junction capacitance
parameters.hint: The diode junction capacitance at a stated bias and frequency (attach V_R and F, e.g. VR = 0 V, f = 1 MHz), in farads (pF normalized: 40 pF is 4e-11). Sets switching speed; printed mainly on IR/signal LEDs used for data links.

parameters.name: ESD withstand voltage
parameters.hint: The human-body-model (HBM) ESD threshold the part withstands, in volts (kV normalized: 2 kV is 2000). InGaN dies are ESD-sensitive; a built-in ESD-protection diode raises this. State the model/class (JS-001 HBM Class) in conditionsVerbatim.

parameters.name: Luminous intensity
parameters.hint: The on-axis luminous intensity of a VISIBLE LED, in candela (mcd normalized: 3100 mcd is 3.1; 54 mcd is 0.054), measured with an eye-response (V-lambda / CIE) weighted sensor at a stated forward current (attach I_F) and, for a multi-die part, an EMITTER. Array over I_F (and EMITTER). The headline spec of an indicator LED. A radiometric IR/UV emitter uses radiant_intensity (W/sr) instead - a part carries one or the other, never both. When a datasheet prints two IV bases (vendor-standard vs CIE-127-traceable), record both as separate measurements with the basis in conditionsVerbatim.

parameters.name: Luminous flux
parameters.hint: The total luminous flux (all directions) of a VISIBLE illumination LED, in lumens, at a stated drive current (attach I_F) and, for white parts, a correlated_color_temperature and color_rendering_index grade. The headline spec of a lighting LED. Array over I_F; a datasheet's flux is also specified per CCT and per CRI grade - carry those as CCT/CRI conditions (or, since they are grade-defining, emit one document per orderable CCT/CRI grade). A binned flux group is a min/max range on the value.

parameters.name: Luminous efficacy
parameters.hint: Luminous flux per electrical watt, in lm/W, at a stated drive point. Derivable as luminous_flux / (VF x IF), but datasheets publish it as a guaranteed, binned headline (e.g. >= 120 lm/W) - store the printed value to preserve that guarantee and its provenance rather than forcing recomputation.

parameters.name: Radiant intensity
parameters.hint: The on-axis radiant intensity of an IR/UV emitter (unweighted radiometric power per unit solid angle), in watts per steradian (mW/sr normalized: 170 mW/sr is 0.17), at a stated forward current (attach I_F, often pulsed - attach PULSE_WIDTH). Array over I_F. The radiometric analogue of luminous_intensity; a part carries one or the other. Never compare an intensity (W/sr) against a radiant_flux (W).

parameters.name: Radiant flux (radiant power)
parameters.hint: The total radiant power (all directions) of an IR/UV emitter, in watts (mW normalized: 40 mW is 0.04; a 16 mW UV-C part is 0.016), at a stated drive current (attach I_F), typically measured in an integrating sphere. Array over I_F. The radiometric analogue of luminous_flux. Distinct from radiant_intensity (W/sr).

parameters.name: Radiant efficiency (wall-plug)
parameters.hint: Radiant flux as a percentage of input electrical power (radiant_flux / (VF x IF) x 100), for an IR/UV emitter. Low for UV-C (a few percent). Store the printed percentage.

parameters.name: Peak wavelength
parameters.hint: The wavelength of maximum spectral power, in metres (nm normalized: 940 nm is 9.4e-7; 630 nm is 6.3e-7; 275 nm is 2.75e-7), at a stated forward current (attach I_F). Distinct from dominant_wavelength (perceived hue) and centroid_wavelength (power-weighted mean) - a part may print more than one. The defining identity of the emitter.

parameters.name: Dominant wavelength
parameters.hint: The perceived-hue wavelength (where the line from the CIE white point through the chromaticity coordinate meets the spectral locus), in metres (nm normalized: 630 nm is 6.3e-7). A VISIBLE-LED quantity; differs from peak_wavelength and is what color-critical indicator/RGB parts bin on. Attach I_F and, for multi-die parts, EMITTER.

parameters.name: Centroid wavelength
parameters.hint: The power-weighted mean wavelength, in metres (nm normalized), at a stated forward current. The metrologically stable figure radiometric (IR/UV) work prefers; distinct from peak (e.g. 860 nm peak vs 850 nm centroid).

parameters.name: Spectral bandwidth (FWHM)
parameters.hint: The full width of the emission spectrum at 50% of peak power (FWHM), in metres (nm normalized: 30 nm is 3e-8; 9 nm is 9e-9). The same unit m as the wavelengths it is a width of. A narrow line (a UV/IR die ~10-30 nm) versus a broad phosphor-converted white spectrum. Attach I_F.

parameters.name: Viewing angle (full angle at half intensity)
parameters.hint: The FULL cone angle between the two off-axis directions where intensity falls to 50% of the on-axis value, in degrees. NORMALIZATION TRAP: vendors print either the full angle 2*theta-1/2 (e.g. 120 deg) OR the half angle theta-1/2 / 'angle of half intensity' (e.g. +/-80 deg or 40 deg). Normalize to the full angle: a printed half-angle is doubled (a printed +/-10 deg half-angle becomes 20 deg). Record which form was printed in conditionsVerbatim. A narrow-beam IR emitter is ~10-20 deg; a wide indicator ~120-140 deg.

parameters.name: Correlated color temperature
parameters.hint: The correlated color temperature of a WHITE LED, in kelvin (2700 K warm, 6500 K cool) - an absolute thermodynamic color point, NEVER converted to or from degC (a 5000 K CCT is not 5000 degC). Grade-defining: one orderable white LED has one nominal CCT, so emit one document per CCT grade; a datasheet that lists flux across several CCTs describes sibling grades. The fine chromaticity sub-bin (MacAdam step) around the nominal is a min/max on chromaticity_x/y.

parameters.name: Color rendering index
parameters.hint: The general color rendering index Ra of a WHITE LED - a dimensionless 0-100 index (unit 1), higher is better (Ra 70 budget, 80 general, 90+ high-CRI). Grade-defining alongside CCT. The 0-100 range vs a 0-1 chromaticity coordinate is disambiguated by the key, not the unit.

parameters.name: Special color rendering index R9 (deep red)
parameters.hint: The special CRI for saturated deep red (R9), a dimensionless index (unit 1) high-CRI lighting parts guarantee separately from Ra because Ra averages R1-R8 and misses red. A negative R9 is common on low-CRI parts.

parameters.name: CIE 1931 chromaticity x
parameters.hint: The CIE 1931 chromaticity x-coordinate of a VISIBLE LED - a dimensionless number (unit 1) in 0-1. Cross-vendor comparable: the ANSI C78.377 quadrangle centers (e.g. 5000 K -> x=0.3447) are identical across Nichia/Samsung/Osram. A binned color sub-rank is a min/max quadrangle around the nominal.

parameters.name: CIE 1931 chromaticity y
parameters.hint: The CIE 1931 chromaticity y-coordinate of a VISIBLE LED - a dimensionless number (unit 1) in 0-1 (e.g. 5000 K -> y=0.3553). Pairs with chromaticity_x to fix the color point.

parameters.name: Thermal resistance, junction to ambient
parameters.hint: Junction-to-ambient thermal resistance, in degC/W (equivalently K/W - the two are numerically identical for a temperature delta and both are legal). Board- and layout-dependent; a small indicator LED is 300-500 degC/W. State the board/pad condition in conditionsVerbatim.

parameters.name: Thermal resistance, junction to solder point
aliases: thermal resistance junction to solder point
junction to solder point thermal resistance
parameters.hint: Junction-to-solder-point thermal resistance, in degC/W (or K/W), the figure a power LED publishes because it is board-independent (a few degC/W for a ceramic power LED). Osram splits a 'real' (measured) from an 'electrical' (efficiency-corrected) value - keep the basis in conditionsVerbatim.

parameters.name: Junction temperature
parameters.hint: The maximum allowable junction temperature (absolute_max), in degC (85-150 typical). The hard reliability limit; the whole thermal design keeps the junction below it.

parameters.name: Operating temperature range
parameters.hint: The ambient temperature range over which the part operates (recommended), in degC. Store min/max bounds.

parameters.name: Storage temperature range
parameters.hint: The non-operating storage temperature range (absolute_max), in degC. Store min/max bounds.

parameters.name: Soldering temperature
parameters.hint: The maximum soldering/reflow temperature (absolute_max), in degC (typically 260), for a stated time and distance from the body - keep those in conditionsVerbatim.

parameters.name: Rise time
parameters.hint: The 10%-90% optical rise time, in seconds (ns normalized: 15 ns is 1.5e-8), at a stated forward current and load (attach I_F, R_L). Printed on IR/data-link emitters; a phosphor-converted white LED's slow phosphor makes this meaningless and it is omitted.

parameters.name: Fall time
parameters.hint: The 90%-10% optical fall time, in seconds (ns normalized), at a stated forward current and load. Pairs with rise_time for data-rate capability.

parameters.name: Temperature coefficient of forward voltage
parameters.hint: The drift of forward voltage with temperature, in V/degC (mV/K normalized: -1.9 mV/K is -1.9e-3; K and degC are identical for a delta). Negative (VF falls as the junction heats). Used to sense junction temperature and to design current sources.

parameters.name: Temperature coefficient of wavelength
parameters.hint: The drift of peak (or dominant) wavelength with temperature, in m/degC (nm/K normalized: 0.2 nm/K is 2e-10 m/degC). Positive (emission red-shifts as the junction heats). Attach which wavelength it applies to and the I_F in conditionsVerbatim.

parameters.name: Temperature coefficient of luminous output
parameters.hint: The relative drift of a VISIBLE part's luminous flux with temperature. Datasheets print it in %/degC (or %/K); normalize to ppm/degC (x1e4: -0.5 %/K is -5000 ppm/degC), the same relative-drift convention the reference/LDO families use. Negative (output falls as the junction heats). An IR/UV part's radiant-output drift uses radiant_flux_temperature_coefficient instead.

parameters.name: Temperature coefficient of radiant output
parameters.hint: The relative drift of an IR/UV part's radiant flux (or radiant intensity) with temperature - the radiometric twin of luminous_flux_temperature_coefficient. Datasheets print it in %/degC (e.g. Vishay 'temperature coefficient of phi_e', -0.6 %/K); normalize to ppm/degC (x1e4: -0.6 %/K is -6000 ppm/degC). Negative. Keeps a radiometric part off the photometric-named luminous key.

parameters.name: Solder-point temperature (max)
parameters.hint: The maximum allowable temperature at the solder joint DURING OPERATION (absolute_max), in degC - the datasheet reference point a thermal designer measures and derates against (ams-OSRAM app note AN085 defines Ts). Distinct from soldering_temperature (the ~260 degC reflow PROCESS limit), junction_temperature (Tj), and operating_temperature_range (ambient). Power/illumination LEDs state it as an operating limit alongside Tj.

parameters.name: Thermal resistance, junction to case
parameters.hint: Junction-to-case thermal resistance, in degC/W (or K/W), quoted by some ceramic power LEDs in addition to or instead of the board-independent junction-to-solder-point figure. State the reference case point in conditionsVerbatim.

parameters.name: Chromaticity Duv (distance from blackbody locus)
parameters.hint: The signed perpendicular offset of a white LED's chromaticity from the Planckian (blackbody) locus - a dimensionless number (unit 1), positive above the locus (greenish) and negative below (pinkish). Modern white binning (ANSI C78.377) specifies the white point as correlated_color_temperature PLUS Duv, the tint that CIE x/y alone does not communicate cleanly. Grade-defining; typically within +/-0.006.

parameters.name: CIE 1976 chromaticity u'
parameters.hint: The CIE 1976 UCS chromaticity u'-coordinate - a dimensionless number (unit 1). The perceptually-uniform plane many white/tunable datasheets and bin maps use for the white point and color step size (a MacAdam-step or Delta-u'v' spec) instead of, or alongside, CIE 1931 x/y.

parameters.name: CIE 1976 chromaticity v'
parameters.hint: The CIE 1976 UCS chromaticity v'-coordinate - a dimensionless number (unit 1). Pairs with chromaticity_u_prime in the perceptually-uniform plane.

parameters.name: Angular color uniformity
parameters.hint: The variation of color over the emission beam that an illumination LED guarantees as a one-bin-over-angle claim - expressed as a Delta-u'v' (dimensionless, unit 1) or, when the datasheet gives it that way, a Delta-CCT (altUnit K). A characterized differentiator on premium white LEDs (Cree XLamp, Lumileds LUXEON).
